subject: Hosted API ingress mapping + rate sanity check
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@velociti.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API ingress mapping + rate sanity check

Hi Liam — great to meet you and María on the call today. Quick recap from my side and the handful of clarifying asks we need to lock a short hosted evaluation (sandbox) for Velociti.

Recap (short):
- Goal: proof-of-concept using Redwood Hosted API for real-time routing suggestions in Velociti’s driver-assist product.
- Target traffic for pilot: daytime peak ~120 qps, average payload ~1.8KB, avg response ~600 tokens.
- Success criteria: <120ms p95 generation for single-turn requests, no errors under 80% peak slice.

Clarifying asks so we can provision the right sandbox slice:
1) Ingress/endpoints: do you prefer a single multiplexed endpoint (multi-tenant prefixing) or dedicated endpoint per environment (staging/prod)? If you’re unsure, tell us which flows are latency-sensitive vs batch so we can recommend an endpoint mapping.
2) Burst behavior: will you expect sudden spikes >2x baseline for short windows (30s-5m)? If yes, approx frequency.
3) Auth & network: will you call from customer devices (mobile) or only from your backend in our US region? If backend-only and you need VPC egress limits, call that out.
4) Data residency & retention: any regulatory constraints beyond standard SOC2?

Next steps we propose:
- Ben will sketch a quick endpoint mapping recommendation + rate ceilings (today).
- Redwood to provision a sandbox endpoint with 150 qps ceiling for two-week trial once we confirm ingress mapping and IP ranges.
- We’ll provide a quickstart checklist (attached) and a short DocuSign to lock trial T&Cs.

Attachments: velociti-map-proposal.pdf (proposal sketch), redwood-quickstart-checklist.xlsx

Would you be able to reply with answers to 1–3 by EOD tomorrow? If not, propose two 30-min slots and Ben/Karthik can join.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.co.le@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@velociti.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co.le@redwood.com>
Cc: María Reyes <maria.reyes@velociti.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API ingress mapping + rate sanity check

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below:
1) Prefer dedicated endpoints per environment (staging + prod). Staging will have lower throughput, prod needs the 120 qps slice.
2) Yes, we see burst events ~3x baseline during dispatch windows, roughly 3–4 times/day for 2–3 minutes.
3) Calls only from our backend (AWS us-east-1). We will need static egress IP ranges for allowlisting.
4) No extra residency constraints (SOC2-compliant is fine).

We can do a 30-min slot on Monday 11/9 at 10am PT if that works to finalize the mapping. María (CTO) will join that call.

—Liam
Liam O'Neill
Head of Product, Velociti AI
liam.oneill@velociti.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@velociti.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.co.le@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API ingress mapping + rate sanity check

Thanks Liam — all helpful answers. A few specifics from our side to make sure expectations align before the Monday call: 

Endpoint mapping recommendation (draft):
- staging.velociti.redwood.run -> staging endpoint (lower throughput, full feature parity)
- prod.velociti.redwood.run -> prod endpoint (dedicated slice, target 150 qps ceiling, 3x burst headroom for short-duration windows)
- prefix-based API key scoping so you can rotate keys per environment without changing DNS.

Rate & capacity notes:
- We can provision a hosted sandbox with a 150 qps nominal ceiling and a burst window that supports 3x for up to 5 minutes, provided we tune batching and token budgets.
- For your payload sizes (~1.8KB req / ~600 token resp) we estimate cost footprint and will include a token estimate in the sandbox runbook.

Network allowlist: send us the AWS egress IP ranges (or VPC NAT IPs) and we’ll whitelist them for the prod endpoint. If you need private connectivity (VPC peering or Private deployment), we can discuss Dedicated/VPC options — best fit if you need predictable multi-node throughput or on-prem constraints.

Proposed Monday agenda (30m):
1) Confirm endpoint mapping and DNS plan (5m)
2) Rate ceilings, bursts, and token budgeting (10m)
3) Sandbox provisioning timeline & drive access to test data (10m)
4) Next steps: DocuSign trial T&Cs and kickoff date (5m)

Drive: I’ve uploaded a short endpoint mapping sketch and the quickstart checklist here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/01VelocitiOnboard
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/VEL-2026-053 (pre-populated trial agreement)

I’ll set the calendar invite for Monday 10am PT and include a short internal preflight checklist to make provisioning quick. Karthik, can you prepare a quick note on batching knobs and recommended token ceilings?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 617-555-0102

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co.le@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@velociti.ai>, María Reyes <maria.reyes@velociti.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API ingress mapping + rate sanity check

Thanks all — invite sent for 11/9 10:00 PT with a Zoom link. Quick final checklist from me before the call so we can provision immediately after:
- Velociti to confirm NAT/egress IPs and a preferred prod DNS name (prod.velociti.redwood.run if acceptable).
- Please sign the trial DocuSign (link above) so legal/t&c are in place; we won’t provision prod credentials until the trial agreement is signed.
- Provide a small sample of non-sensitive test payloads (S3/Drive link) so we can pre-seed KV/prefix caching guidance.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-checklist.xlsx (action list), velociti-docusign-signature-link.txt (DocuSign link copy)

If you want to consider Dedicated (reserved capacity) instead of Hosted after the trial, we can run a short throughput exercise in week 2 to show where Dedicated would materially reduce p95 latency under sustained 500+ qps. For now, Hosted sandbox with the requested ceilings will validate the integration.

See you on the call.

Best —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.co.le@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
